samples.summary: New `movedSpillAnchors` → `clearSpillBlockers` branch in `moveRangeTo` has no test
samples.evidence: The delta adds, in `moveRangeTo`, a collection of cells with `spillRows/spillCols/spillBlocked` (line 2393) and a `clearSpillBlockers(sref)` pass at line 2410, justified by the comment 'A moving anchor's blocker registrations name its old sref'. No test moves a *blocked* spill anchor. In packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts the move tests either move the BLOCKER cell (line 202) or move a successfully-spilling MUNIT anchor (line 284); neither has a live `spillBlockers` registration keyed to the moving anchor, so the `clearSpillBlockers` line could be deleted and all tests would still pass (the MUNIT anchor is unblocked, so its registration map is empty). A regression here (stale registration re-queuing the anchor's abandoned position) would be invisible to the suite.

samples.summary: Only one of the two new ghost branches in `moveRangeTo` is tested (anchor-outside-range ghost move is uncovered)
samples.evidence: Line 2387-2390 splits ghosts into `staleGhosts` (anchor moves with them) and 'ghost owned by an anchor outside the range stays read-only where it is'. The new test 'drag-moving a spill leaves no ghosts behind at the source' (calculation.test.ts:284) covers only the stale branch — it moves the whole MUNIT block including its anchor. No test drag-moves a sub-range that contains ghosts whose anchor is NOT in the range (e.g. moving B1:B2 of a MUNIT(2) at A1), so the behaviour that the ghosts stay put at the source and nothing ghost-derived is written at the destination is unverified.

samples.summary: Refusal-notice tests bypass `Worksheet.initialize`, so the wiring the diff refactored is not covered
samples.evidence: `wire()` (worksheet-notice.test.ts:21-28) calls `Worksheet.prototype.setOnNotice` and the private `bindRefusalNotices` against a bare `{}` context rather than a real Worksheet. That exercises `refusalMessage` mapping, but nothing asserts that `initialize` still calls `bindRefusalNotices` (src/view/worksheet.ts:415). If that call were dropped, refusals would go nowhere in production and every test in this file would still pass — which is exactly the wiring the diff moved.

samples.summary: `hands Spreadsheet.onNotice through to the worksheet` asserts only that a mock was called
samples.evidence: The test builds `const worksheet = { setOnNotice: vi.fn() }`, invokes `Spreadsheet.prototype.onNotice.call({worksheet}, callback)` and asserts `expect(worksheet.setOnNotice).toHaveBeenCalledWith(callback)`. The real Worksheet — the only thing that could break — is mocked away; the assertion restates the one-line delegation it just called, so it cannot fail for any behavioural reason.

samples.summary: `stays silent until a host registers a notice callback` asserts nothing about silence
samples.evidence: The only assertion is `await expect(sheet.moveRangeTo(...)).resolves.toBeUndefined()`. `moveRangeTo` returns `Promise<void>`, so `toBeUndefined()` holds whether the refusal fired, whether the move succeeded, or whether the refusal path was never reached. The test's stated behaviour ('must not throw when no callback is registered') is only covered incidentally; it would pass even if the refusal were never emitted.

samples.summary: Cut-paste of a range containing a spill (anchor and/or ghosts) is untested despite the delta touching that loop
samples.evidence: The delta adds blocker consumption to the cut-paste source-clearing loop (sheet.ts:2254-2265) but, unlike `moveRangeTo`, leaves the `if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;` guard with no stale-ghost handling and no `clearSpillBlockers` for a cut spill anchor. The new cut-paste test (calculation.test.ts:251) cuts a plain 'BLOCKER' string only. No test cuts and pastes a spilling anchor, so whether ghosts are left orphaned at the source or copied to the destination by the cut path is unverified.

verdict.reason: The `movedSpillAnchors` collection (sheet.ts:2385-2395) and the `clearSpillBlockers(sref)` pass (sheet.ts:2410-2412) only have observable effect when the moved cell is a *blocked* anchor: registrations are created solely on the blocked path (calculator.ts:115-117) and are cleared on every successful spill (calculator.ts:130), so `clearSpillBlockers` is a no-op for an unblocked anchor (sheet.ts:983-987). I searched repo-wide: `moveRangeTo` is exercised in only three test files (calculation.test.ts, merge.test.ts, view/worksheet-notice.test.ts), and only calculation.test.ts touches spill at all. Its move cases move the BLOCKER cell (calculation.test.ts:202-225, and the cut/merge/autofill variants at 251, 263, 310) or a successfully-spilling MUNIT anchor with an empty registration map (calculation.test.ts:284-308). No test moves a cell with a live `spillBlockers` entry keyed to it, no test inspects `spillBlockers`, and there are no other test locations (no sheets .spec.ts files, no e2e dir, no other file referencing MINVERSE/MUNIT/MMULT). Line 2411 could be deleted and the suite would still pass, so this behavior change ships with no meaningful coverage — major under the missing-tests rubric.

finding.summary: New view-layer refusal→message plumbing (`refusalMessage`, `setOnNotice`, `Spreadsheet.onNotice`, sheet-view toast) has no test whatsoever
finding.evidence: The user-visible half of this change is the message text and the wiring Sheet.setOnRefusal → Worksheet.onNoticeCallback → Spreadsheet.onNotice → toast.error. Grepping the whole repo for `onNotice|setOnNotice|refusalMessage` returns only src files plus model-level `setOnRefusal` uses in tests; no test file references them. packages/sheets/test/view/ contains many Worksheet tests (worksheet-mouse, worksheet-keymap, worksheet-mobile-edit …), so this layer is testable, yet nothing asserts that a refused drag produces the string "Can't move part of a merged cell…" or that the callback fires at all. In particular `refusalMessage` maps 'merge-autofill' via a `default:` branch, so a future refusal kind would silently get the autofill text with no test to catch it.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file the reviewer missed refutes each specific claim: packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-notice.test.ts. (a) "no test file references onNotice/setOnNotice/refusalMessage" is false — lines 11, 25, 130-139 reference setOnNotice, onNoticeCallback and Spreadsheet.onNotice. (b) "nothing asserts a refused drag produces 'Can't move part of a merged cell…'" is false — lines 37-54 assert that exact string (matching worksheet.ts:101) after a real moveRangeTo on a real Sheet/MemStore. (c) The 'merge-autofill' default: branch the finding singles out as uncatchable IS tested at lines 78-90, asserting "Can't autofill across merged cells. Unmerge them first." (worksheet.ts:108); merge-dest-partial is covered at 56-76. (d) "or that the callback fires at all" — covered, plus a negative case (lines 92-108: a successful move yields [] and the data actually lands) and an unregistered-callback case (110-128). The tests are not vacuous or over-mocked: wire() invokes the real Worksheet.prototype.setOnNotice and the real private bindRefusalNotices (worksheet.ts:862-866, the same method initialize calls at worksheet.ts:417) against a real model, so they fail if the message strings or the setOnRefusal to onNoticeCallback wiring break. Spreadsheet.onNotice to worksheet.setOnNotice is covered at 130-140. The file is collected by the default vitest include (packages/sheets/vite.config.ts sets no include override). Only the frontend toast.error registration (sheet-view.tsx:1020) is uncovered — a one-line callback registration, far narrower than the "no test whatsoever" claim and not blocking on its own.
